onboarding.welcome.title: Welcome to MintCat
onboarding.welcome.description: MintCat is a mod manager and integration tool for Deep Rock Galactic and more. Here's a quick overview of each section.
onboarding.configImport.title: Import Config
onboarding.configImport.description: If you have config from an older version or another PC, you can import it here. Click the button below to open the config import window, then close it and click Next.
onboarding.gameSelect.title: Select Game
onboarding.gameSelect.description: Choose the game to manage and set its install path. Click the highlighted "Select Game" button below to open the dialog, then close it and click Next.
onboarding.home.title: Home · Mod List
onboarding.home.description: Manage your mods, groups, enable/disable mods, and run "Integrate" to install the current profile into the game.
onboarding.switchProfile.title: Switch profile
onboarding.switchProfile.description: Switch between different mod profiles here. You can create multiple profiles and change between them anytime.
onboarding.save.title: Save
onboarding.save.description: After enabling/disabling mods or changing groups, click Save to write the current profile; then click Launch in the title bar to install into the game.
onboarding.addMod.title: Add Mod
onboarding.addMod.description: Click here to open the Add Mod dialog. You can add mods from local files, mod.io links, or clipboard to the current profile.
onboarding.launch.title: Launch
onboarding.launch.description: Click here to integrate the current profile into the game and then launch.
onboarding.switchGame.title: Switch game
onboarding.switchGame.description: Click here to select or switch the current game (e.g. Deep Rock Galactic, Rogue Core). Each game has its own mod profiles.
onboarding.modio.title: mod.io · Search & Add
onboarding.modio.description: Search and download mods from mod.io, ModCat, Nexus Mods, Thunderstore, or add from local files.
onboarding.setting.title: Settings
onboarding.setting.description: Configure game path, theme, language, cloud backup, and more. We recommend choosing your game and install path here first.
onboarding.userSettings.title: User Settings
onboarding.userSettings.description: Click here to open User Settings and manage account sign-in and access keys for mod.io, ModCat, and other platforms for searching and downloading mods.
onboarding.end.title: Get Started
onboarding.end.description: That's it. You can find help or send feedback in Settings anytime. Enjoy!

conflict.noEffect: This mod has no effect: every file it contains is replaced by a mod above it.
conflict.noEffectMods: {{count}} mod(s) have no effect (every file is replaced by a mod above):
conflict.rating.harmlessHint: Nothing is lost: both mods have the exact same file, or the winning mod's version makes every change this one makes (compared with the game's original).
conflict.rating.cosmeticHint: Looks or sounds (textures, materials, meshes, audio, effects): only the winning mod's version shows. Usually nothing breaks. Estimated from asset names.
conflict.rating.gameplayHint: Blueprints, item/data assets or maps: the losing mod's changes to these are lost, so it may not work (fully or partly). Unrecognized files count as gameplay to be safe. Estimated from asset names.
conflict.summary.noEffect: No effect: every file is replaced by mods above it
conflict.summary.losesGameplay: Partly overridden: mods above it replace some of its gameplay files
conflict.summary.losesCosmetic: Mods above it replace some of its looks/sounds
conflict.summary.harmless: Harmless: only shares identical files or the same changes
conflict.summary.winsAll: Wins: it's above every mod it shares files with, so its versions are used
conflict.summary.redundant: Redundant: every file is replaced, but the mods above make the same changes
conflict.comparingChanges: Comparing what each mod changes in the shared files…
conflict.legend.title: What the colors mean
conflict.legend.noEffect: Every file of this mod is replaced by mods above it, and they do something different. The mod does nothing while it stays below them.
conflict.legend.losesGameplay: Mods above it replace some of its gameplay files (blueprints, item data, maps…). The parts of this mod in those files won't work; the rest still does.
conflict.legend.losesCosmetic: Mods above it replace some of its textures, models, sounds or effects. The mod works, but those parts look or sound like the other mod's.
conflict.legend.redundant: Every file is replaced, but the mods above make exactly the same changes, so nothing is lost. This mod could be turned off.
conflict.legend.winsAll: It's above every mod it shares files with, so its versions are used. Check the mods it overrides.
conflict.legend.harmless: It only shares files that are identical, or that make the same changes. Nothing to do.
conflict.legend.how: A file can only come from one mod. When two mods have the same file, the one higher in the list wins and the other mod's version is never loaded. Each mod's version is compared with the game's original part by part (settings, functions, events) to tell what is really lost.
conflict.legend.ratings: File tags: Gameplay = blueprints, data or maps (code and settings); Cosmetic = textures, models, sounds, effects; Harmless = nothing lost. Contents tags: Identical, Same changes (nothing lost), Different parts (the losing mod's changes are lost but don't clash — both could work if combined), Clash (both change the same thing).
conflict.group.modFiles: Mod library files (not in the game)
conflict.outcome.identicalHint: Both mods have exactly the same file.
conflict.outcome.sameChangesHint: The files differ, but the winning mod's version makes every change the other makes. Nothing is lost.
conflict.outcome.separateHint: They change different parts of this file. Only one file can be used, so the losing mod's changes here are lost — they don't clash with the winner's, so both could work if the file were combined.
conflict.outcome.clashHint: Both change the same parts differently. Only the winning mod's version of those parts is used.
conflict.outcome.unknownHint: The contents weren't compared (not an asset file, couldn't be read, or the game's files weren't available). Rated by the file's name and folder.
conflict.verdict.nothingLost: Nothing is lost: the shared files are identical, or {{winner}} makes the same changes {{loser}} does.
conflict.verdict.audio: One of them is a separate audio pak, so the game decides which sound plays, not the list order. To be sure, turn one off.
conflict.verdict.copies: They have exactly the same files with different content — most likely two versions or variants of the same mod. Only {{winner}} is used; keep the one you want and turn the other off.
conflict.verdict.replacedWhole: {{winner}} has every file {{loser}} has, so {{loser}} does nothing while it's below. If {{loser}} is the one you want (newer, or a different variant), move it above; otherwise turn it off.
conflict.verdict.addon: {{winner}} replaces only some of {{loser}}'s files — usually a patch, add-on or variant made for {{loser}}. Keeping {{winner}} above is normally right.
conflict.verdict.combinable: They change different parts of the same files. Only one copy of a file can be used, so {{loser}}'s changes in these files are lost, even though they don't clash with {{winner}}'s. Put the one whose changes matter more to you on top.
conflict.verdict.clash: They change the same parts of these files in different ways, so they can't both work there. Only {{winner}}'s version is used.
conflict.verdict.cosmetic: Only looks or sounds: you'll see or hear {{winner}}'s version of these. Put the one you prefer on top.
conflict.verdict.unclear: {{winner}} replaces some of {{loser}}'s gameplay files and their contents couldn't be compared, so parts of {{loser}} may not work.
conflict.relation.duplicateHint: Both mods consist of exactly the same files.
conflict.relation.loserInsideHint: {{winner}} has all of {{loser}}'s files (and maybe more).
conflict.relation.winnerInsideHint: {{winner}} has only some of {{loser}}'s files: it may be a patch, add-on or variant for it, or a different mod that changes the same things.
conflict.relation.libraryHint: All shared files are files the game doesn't have: both mods bundle the same helper files (a library or framework). Usually the newest copy should be on top.
conflict.relation.partialHint: They share some of their files.
conflict.action.done.swap: {{mod}} is now above {{other}} — click Deploy to apply it to the game
conflict.action.done.disable: Turned off {{mod}} — click Deploy to apply it to the game
conflict.short.redundant: All files are replaced by {{winners}}, which make the same changes
conflict.short.harmless: Only shares identical files or the same changes
conflict.effect.files: {{total}} files: {{own}} only in this mod, {{won}} shared and used, {{replaced}} replaced by mods above
conflict.effect.covered: {{count}} more replaced, but nothing is lost there (same file or same changes).
conflict.report.modsSummary: {{mods}} mods share files ({{pairs}} pairs): {{noEffect}} with no effect, {{gameplay}} partly overridden, {{cosmetic}} with looks/sounds replaced, {{redundant}} redundant.
conflict.report.notCompared: The game's own files couldn't be read (check the game path in settings), so mods are only compared with each other, not with the game's originals, and some ratings are estimated from file names.
conflict.diff.title: {{asset}}: what each mod changes
conflict.diff.noContext: Run the conflict check again to compare this file.
conflict.diff.notInGame: The game doesn't have this file: mods added it. The mods' versions are compared with each other.
conflict.diff.noGame: The game's original couldn't be read in detail, so the mods are only compared with each other.
conflict.diff.shallow: This kind of file can only be compared object by object (no setting-level detail).
conflict.diff.summary: Compared with the game: {{winner}} (used) changes {{winnerCount}} part(s), {{loser}} changes {{loserCount}}.
conflict.diff.lostSummary: {{count}} of {{loser}}'s changes are lost here, because only {{winner}}'s file is used.
conflict.diff.lostSummaryClash: {{count}} of {{loser}}'s changes are lost here, because only {{winner}}'s file is used; {{clash}} of them clash with {{winner}}'s changes.
conflict.diff.noneLost: Nothing of {{loser}} is lost in this file.
conflict.diff.separateHint: None of these clash with {{winner}}'s changes: both mods could work together if this file were combined. Until then, put the mod whose changes you want on top.
conflict.diff.resultHint.lost: Only {{loser}} changes this; its change is lost because {{winner}}'s file is used.
conflict.diff.resultHint.kept: Only {{winner}} changes this; its change is used.
conflict.diff.resultHint.clash: Both change this, differently. {{winner}}'s version is used.

help.folderColors: Like separator colors in Amethyst: right-click a folder and pick a color. The folder bar takes the color and the mods inside it (and in its subfolders without a color of their own) get a stripe of it.
help.linkIcons: Shows an icon in front of each local mod: linked to a Pak Hub post automatically, downloaded from Pak Hub, linked by you (right-click → Link to Pak Hub post…), or not linked. Hover an icon to see which.
help.autoLinkColor: Shows the names of local mods that MINTCAT linked to their Pak Hub (repository) post automatically, by file name, in this color.
multi.checkboxHint: Select several mods. Tip: Ctrl-click mods (or a folder) to pick them, Shift-click to pick a range, Ctrl+A for all; Esc clears, Delete removes them from the list.
cloudBackup.help: Uploads a copy of MINTCAT's database (mod lists, profiles and settings, including your mod.io login) to the MINTCAT developers' own server, so you can restore it later or on another PC. It only works with a supporter key from the MINTCAT developers (vip.mintcat.work), entered as "MintCat OAuth" in User Settings (top right). It doesn't connect to Google Drive or other storage services.
help.mintcatProxy: Lets mod.io requests go through the MINTCAT developers' relay server, for places where mod.io is slow or blocked. Auto: connect directly and use the relay only when that fails. Enabled: relay first. Disabled: never use it.
help.networkProxy: Sends MINTCAT's internet traffic through a proxy, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890. Leave it empty to connect directly.
help.testConnection: Checks whether each MINTCAT server can be reached, and how fast.
help.resourceServer: Which MINTCAT server its helper files and online features come from: mainland China or international. Auto picks the one that answers.
help.devTools: Opens the developer console of MINTCAT's window. Only useful for troubleshooting.
help.compress: Compresses the one combined pak that MINTCAT writes into the game's Paks folder when you install. It takes less disk space, but installing takes longer and the game has to unpack it while loading. Your own mod files aren't changed.
help.ue4ss: Installs UE4SS, a script loader that some mods need (their mod page says so), into the game folder when you install mods. If none of your mods need it, turn it off and it isn't installed.
help.releaseChannel: Which release of MINTCAT's helper files to download, such as the UE4SS loader it puts in the game folder. Stable is the safe choice. This Linux build gets its own updates from GitHub, so this doesn't affect app updates.
help.descriptionHover: Hovering a mod's name in the list shows its description from mod.io (or the post text, for local mods linked to a Pak Hub post).
help.clipboard: When you copy a mod link or the path of a .pak/.zip file anywhere, MINTCAT opens Add Mod with it.
help.clearCache: Deletes everything in the download folder (downloaded mod files, images, avatars). Your mod list stays as it is; mod files are downloaded again the next time you install. To pick which files go, use the Downloads page.
help.cacheDir: Where downloaded mod files (mod.io, Nexus Mods, ModCat), thumbnails and avatars are kept. The Downloads page (left bar) lists them and lets you delete the ones you don't need.
help.mintImport: Adds the mods from a mint mod_data.json to the current profile, each mint group into the folder with the same name. Mods already in the list are skipped and nothing is removed. You can also drop the file onto the window.
help.importConfig: Imports a saved config from mint's own config folder (~/.config/drg-mod-integration/config) or from an older MINTCAT version: its settings, mod.io login and profiles (added as new profiles). To add the mods from a mint mod_data.json saved anywhere to the current profile, use Import mint mod list.
help.configDir: Where MINTCAT keeps its database: your mod lists, profiles and settings. Back up this folder to keep your setup.
mintImport.dropNotJson: Drop a mint mod_data.json, .pak/.zip files or mod links here.
mintImport.dropLocal: To add .pak/.zip files, open Add Mod → Local and drop them there.
mintImport.configHint: This copies the config's settings (such as the game folder and mod.io login) and adds its profiles as new profiles. To only add the mods from a mint mod_data.json to your current profile, use Import from mint.
mintImport.configNone: No saved config was found in mint's config folder (~/.config/drg-mod-integration/config) or from older MINTCAT versions. If you have a mint mod_data.json somewhere else, import its mods with Import from mint.
advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.hint: Shows settings most people never need: release channel, Compress Mod Pak, developer tools, network and server settings, the MINTCAT supporters' cloud backup (always shown once a MintCat supporter key is set) and the notifications bell. Their defaults work without changes.
backup.title: Backups
backup.help: A backup is one .zip with your mod lists, profiles, folders and MINTCAT settings, the settings files mods keep in the game folder, and (optionally) your local .pak files. Save it to a folder — for example one that Dropbox's or MEGA's sync app keeps in the cloud — or straight to Google Drive, Dropbox or MEGA through rclone. Nothing goes through MINTCAT's servers.
backup.folderHelp: Any folder. Pick one that Dropbox, MEGA or another sync app syncs and the backups end up in that cloud too.
backup.accountHelp: Cloud accounts set up in rclone. Connect account adds Google Drive, Dropbox or MEGA. Any other service rclone supports (OneDrive, pCloud, Proton Drive…) works too: set it up with "rclone config" in a terminal and it shows up here.
backup.noAccounts: No accounts yet — use Connect account
backup.rclone.install: Cloud accounts are reached through rclone, a free program for cloud storage. On CachyOS / Arch Linux install it with:
backup.rclone.installOther: Other systems: see rclone.org/install. Then press Check again.
backup.includeDatabase: Mod lists, profiles and MINTCAT settings
backup.autoHelp: While MINTCAT is open it makes a backup once a day or once a week and removes older automatic backups beyond the number to keep. Backups you make yourself are never removed automatically.
backup.chooseFirst: Choose where to save backups first
backup.saveCopy: Save a copy on this PC…
backup.connect.title: Connect a cloud account
backup.connect.about.drive: You sign in to Google in your browser. MINTCAT (through rclone) only gets access to files it creates in your Drive, not the rest of it.
backup.connect.about.dropbox: You sign in to Dropbox in your browser and allow rclone to use your Dropbox.
backup.connect.about.mega: MEGA uses your email and password. They are stored (scrambled) in rclone's config file, not in MINTCAT. If your account uses two-step login and connecting fails, use MEGA's sync app with the Folder option instead.
backup.connect.name: Name in rclone
backup.connect.nameHelp: How this account is called in rclone's list
backup.connect.nameTaken: Use letters, numbers, - or _, and a name that isn't used yet
backup.connect.waiting: Finish signing in in your browser, then come back here.
backup.restore.title: Restore the backup from {{date}}
backup.restore.containsText: {{mods}} mods, {{profiles}} profile(s), {{settings}} mod settings files, {{paks}} local .pak files
backup.restore.database: Mod lists, profiles and MINTCAT settings
backup.restore.databaseHelp: Replaces what MINTCAT has now. It takes effect when MINTCAT restarts; the current data is kept as mintcat.sqlite.bak in MINTCAT's config folder.
backup.restore.localModsHelp: {{missing}} missing from this PC will be put back where they were ({{size}}). {{present}} that are already there are left alone.
backup.restore.modsElsewhere: Some .pak files couldn't go back to their old folder and were saved in {{path}}. Right-click one of those mods → Locate missing file… and pick it there; MINTCAT offers to update the others from the same folder.
backup.restore.restartText: The mod lists, profiles and settings from the backup are put in place when MINTCAT starts again.
modSettings.title: Mod settings files
modSettings.help: Mods that have their own options save them in the game folder (FSD/Saved/SaveGames). Export them to a zip to keep or share, or import them from a zip or another copy of the folder. Your game progress save (…_Player.sav) is never exported or replaced, and files an import would replace are copied to MINTCAT's data folder first.
modSettings.folderHelp: Found from the game path set in MINTCAT: <game>/FSD/Saved/SaveGames.
modSettings.folderMissing: The folder doesn't exist yet. Start the game once with your mods.
modSettings.noGamePath: Set the game path first (Select Game) to use mod settings files.
modSettings.protectedHint: Your game progress save and its backups are in the same folder. They are never exported, imported or replaced.
modSettings.sameFolder: That is the game's own settings folder. Pick another copy (for example from another PC or a backup).
modSettings.protectedNote: {{count}} game progress save file(s) found here are skipped: your progress is never replaced.
modSettings.nothingFound: No settings files were found there.
modSettings.defaultPickHint: New files and files newer than yours are picked; tick others to replace them too. Replaced files are copied to MINTCAT's data folder (mod-settings-backups) first.
modSettings.selectedSummary: {{count}} selected · {{replacing}} would replace a file you have
modSettings.replacedSaved: The files that were replaced were copied to {{path}}
modSettings.closeGame: Close Deep Rock Galactic first: the game would overwrite the files when it exits.
modSettings.statusHelp.new: You don't have this file yet.
modSettings.statusHelp.newer: This copy was saved later than yours.
modSettings.statusHelp.older: This copy was saved before yours; importing it goes back to the older settings.
modSettings.statusHelp.changed: The files differ and the dates can't be compared.
modSettings.statusHelp.same: Same size and date as yours.
modSettings.statusHelp.protected: Your game progress save. MINTCAT never replaces it.
keptCopies.settingsHelp: Before an import replaces one of your mod settings files, MINTCAT copies it into its data folder (one folder per import). Delete the copies when you don't need them any more.
keptCopies.databaseHelp: Restoring a backup keeps the database it replaced as mintcat.sqlite.bak in MINTCAT's config folder, in case the restore wasn't what you wanted. Delete it when you don't need it any more.
keptCopies.settingsConfirmTitle: Delete the copies of replaced files?
keptCopies.settingsConfirm: This deletes {{files}} file(s) ({{size}}) that MINTCAT copied before imports replaced them. The mod settings files in the game folder aren't touched.
keptCopies.databaseConfirm: This deletes the database kept from before the last restore ({{size}}). The database MINTCAT uses now isn't touched.
gameConfig.title: Game config files
gameConfig.help: The game's own settings files (Engine.ini, Game.ini, GameUserSettings.ini, …). Edit them here; every earlier version is kept, so a change can be undone. Changes apply the next time the game starts.
gameConfig.folderHelp: Where the game keeps them. Under Proton that is usually in the game's prefix (steamapps/compatdata/548430/pfx/…/AppData/Local/FSD/Saved/Config/WindowsNoEditor); some setups use the game folder. When both exist, the one the game changed last is picked first.
gameConfig.folderMissing: The folder doesn't exist yet. Start the game once, or create a file here.
gameConfig.folderNotCreated: This folder doesn't exist yet. The game creates it on its first start; creating a file here also creates it.
gameConfig.noGamePath: MINTCAT doesn't know where the game is. Set the game path first.
gameConfig.readOnlyHelp: The game can't change a read-only file, so tweaks in it stay. MINTCAT can still save it. Settings changed in the game's menus that live in that file won't be kept while it's on.
gameConfig.unlockedNow: {{name}} can be changed by the game again
gameConfig.saved: {{name}} saved; the earlier version was kept
gameConfig.editorNote: Close the game before saving: it reads these files when it starts and can write over them when it exits. The file as it is now is kept before saving (Ctrl+S saves).
gameConfig.earlier: Earlier versions ({{count}}): load one into the editor
gameConfig.backupLoaded: Earlier version loaded. Save to use it.
gameConfig.changedSinceOpened: {{name}} was changed after you opened it (the game may have written it). Save your version over it? The current one is kept as an earlier version.
keptCopies.configHelp: Each time a game config file is saved here, MINTCAT keeps the version it replaced (the newest 20 of each file). Delete them when you don't need them any more.
keptCopies.configConfirm: This deletes {{files}} earlier version(s) ({{size}}) of config files MINTCAT saved. The config files the game uses aren't touched.
repoUpdate.reviewSummary: Repository mods: {{found}} with a newer file to review, {{linked}} newly linked
updateReview.title: Newer files found for {{count}} local mod(s)
updateReview.intro: Nothing has been replaced. Tick the mods to update and, where several files were found, pick one. A new version can be uploaded under a new name or in another post, so check who posted it and read the notes.
updateReview.samePostHelp: Posted in the post this mod is linked to.
updateReview.otherPostHelp: Found in a different post by searching for the file name. It may be someone else's edit of the mod: check the post before replacing.
updateReview.otherUploaderHelp: Posted by someone other than the person who posted the version you have.
updateReview.renamedHelp: Has a different name that looks like a new version of your file (for example _v6). Your mod keeps its place, folder and on/off state.
updateReview.notes: Notes posted with the new version(s) ({{count}})
updateReview.unknownVersionHelp: Your file doesn't match any upload in the post (it may be an older or edited copy), so it can't be told whether this one is newer. Not picked by default.
updateReview.safety: Your own .pak files are never changed: the new file is downloaded into MINTCAT's data folder and the mod points to it. Only files that MINTCAT itself downloaded earlier are removed when they're no longer used.
backup.titleBar.setup: Choose where to save backups first: Settings → Backups.
iconPicker.imageHint: PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF, SVG or ICO. It's resized to 128 px and stored in MINTCAT's settings, so moving the file later is fine.
iconPicker.notImage: That file couldn't be opened as an image.
iconPicker.menuEntry: Also use it for MINTCAT's entry in the app menu and taskbar
iconPicker.menuEntryHint: Changes only the icon line of {{file}} (made by your AppImage manager); picking the default puts its own icon back. MINTCAT sets it again at start if an update replaced the entry.
iconPicker.noMenuEntry: No app menu entry for this AppImage was found, so only the window icon changes.
iconPicker.menuEntryFailed: The app menu entry's icon couldn't be changed: {{reason}}
help.titleBarIcons: The icon next to the MINTCAT name and the profile picture at the top right: pick a built-in icon or any image file. You can also click the app icon, or right-click the profile picture.
usageStats.label: Usage statistics
help.usageStats: Lets the MINTCAT developers count app starts and pages opened through umami.is (it records screen size, language, system and country; no mod lists or files). Turned off, nothing is sent.
deploy.button.deployingHelp: Putting the enabled mods into the game…
deploy.button.doneHelp: The game has this list: {{count}} mod(s) deployed {{when}}. Click to deploy again.
deploy.button.doneHelpNoTime: The game has this list. Click to deploy again.
deploy.button.missingHelp: The list was deployed, but its mods aren't in the game folder any more (a game update or "Verify integrity of game files" can remove them). Click to put them back.
deploy.button.pendingHelp: The game doesn't have your latest changes yet. Click to put the enabled mods into the game (Save Changes).
deploy.button.uninstalledHelp: No mods are in the game: you uninstalled them {{when}}, so the game starts without mods. Click to deploy the enabled mods again.
deploy.button.uninstalledHelpNoTime: No mods are in the game: you uninstalled them, so the game starts without mods. Click to deploy the enabled mods again.
deploy.button.notDeployedHelp: This list hasn't been deployed yet, so the game starts without these mods. Click to put the enabled mods into the game.
deploy.button.otherProfileHelp: The game has profile "{{profile}}"'s mods (deployed {{when}}), not this one's. Click to deploy this profile.
help.confirmDelete: Every delete asks first: mods, folders, profiles, backups, kept copies, repositories, the cache. Turn it off to delete right away. A folder that still has mods still asks whether they go too.
deleteConfirm.mod: Remove "{{name}}" from the list? (Files you added yourself are never deleted.)
deleteConfirm.mods: Remove {{count}} mod(s) from the list? (Files you added yourself are never deleted.)
deleteConfirm.repository: Remove the repository "{{name}}"? Mods you added from it stay in your list.
profile.deleteAsk: Its mod list, folders and settings are removed, along with Pak Hub downloads no other profile uses. You can keep a backup of it first: backups are listed here, where you can restore or delete them.
profile.backupFailed: Couldn't back up the profile, so it wasn't deleted.
profile.deleteFailed: Couldn't delete the profile, so nothing of it was removed.
profile.backupsHelp: Profiles you deleted with "Keep a backup". Restore makes one a profile again; Delete removes the backup for good.
profile.restoredMissing: {{count}} mod(s) of it are no longer in MINTCAT and were left out.
profile.backupDeleteAsk: Delete the backup of "{{name}}" for good?
log.profile.backedUp: Kept a backup of profile "{{name}}" ({{count}} mods)
log.profile.restored: Restored profile "{{name}}" from its backup ({{count}} mods)
deploy.button.deletedProfileHelp: The game has the mods of a profile you deleted since (deployed {{when}}). Click to deploy this profile.
deploy.log.started: Deploying {{count}} enabled mod(s) ({{disabled}} disabled) from profile "{{profile}}" to {{game}}
deploy.log.foreignPaks: {{count}} other .pak file(s) in the game's Paks folder
deploy.log.foreignPaksKept: Deploying anyway, the other .pak files stay where they are
deploy.log.upToDate: Nothing to do: the game already has these {{count}} mod(s)
deploy.log.removedPrevious: Took the previously deployed mods out of the game
deploy.log.done: Deployed {{count}} mod(s) to the game in {{seconds}} s
deploy.log.reordered: Install order changed since the last deploy
deploy.log.sameMods: Same mods in the same order as the last deploy
deploy.log.uninstalled: Uninstalled all mods from the game ({{count}} had been deployed)
deploy.log.uninstalledUnknown: Uninstalled all mods from the game
deploy.log.uninstallFailed: Uninstalling the mods from the game failed: {{reason}}
deploy.log.uninstallNoGame: Can't uninstall: the game's folder isn't set or wasn't found
log.list.cleanedMissing: Removed {{count}} local mod(s) whose files are missing
log.backup.restoredDatabase: mod lists and settings (after a restart)
log.settings.replacedKept: The files they replaced were copied aside first
log.kept.deletedSettings: Deleted the copies of replaced mod settings files
log.kept.deletedConfig: Deleted the earlier versions of the game's config files
log.kept.deletedDatabase: Deleted the database copy kept from the last restore
log.clipboard.copied: Copied link or file noticed ({{count}}): opening Add Mod
log.clipboard.copiedAgain: The same link or file was copied again ({{count}}) and isn't in the list: opening Add Mod
log.conflicts.found: Conflict check: {{count}} mod(s) share files with another mod
deploy.log.uninstallRefused: the game folder couldn't be changed (is the game running?)
nexusmods.windowClosed: The Nexus Mods window was closed before a download started, so nothing was added.
userSetting.nexusChecking: Checking the key with Nexus Mods…
userSetting.nexusKeyRejected: Nexus Mods didn't accept this key (or couldn't be reached).
userSetting.nexusPremium: {{name}} · Premium: files download straight through the Nexus API, no web page needed.
userSetting.nexusFree: {{name}} · Free account: Nexus only gives free accounts their files through its website, so each download opens the mod's page in a small window.
userSetting.nexusWebsiteLogin: That window remembers your Nexus website login, like a browser does, until you sign out.
userSetting.nexusSignOutConfirm: Remove MINTCAT's Nexus Mods website login (its cookies)? Your API key stays. The next download that needs the website asks you to log in again.
userSetting.nexusSignedOut: Signed out of the Nexus Mods website ({{count}} cookie(s) removed)
userSetting.nexusSignOutFailed: Could not sign out of the Nexus Mods website
userSetting.keysInKeyring: Keys are kept in your system keyring (KWallet / GNOME Keyring), encrypted and unlocked with your login, not in MINTCAT's files.
userSetting.keysInFile: No system keyring answered, so keys are saved in MINTCAT's settings database, in a folder only your user account can open.
repo.removeLinkedNote: {{count}} of your mods came from it or are linked to it. MINTCAT won't look for newer uploads of them until you add this repository again (that links them again).
sort.title: Sort
repo.cantRemoveLast: Browse Mods needs at least one source
repo.hideBuiltInConfirm: Remove {{name}} from the Browse Mods source list? This only hides it there: mods you added from {{name}} stay in your lists and keep updating. You can add it back under "Add or remove sources…".
repo.hiddenBuiltIn: Removed {{name}} from the Browse Mods sources
repo.shownBuiltIn: Added {{name}} back to the Browse Mods sources
newFolder.title: New folder
newFolder.taken: There's already a folder called "{{name}}" there
newFolder.buttonTip: Make a new folder for the mods you're adding (it's created when you press OK)
newFolder.failed: Could not create the new folder: {{reason}}
downloads.title: Downloads
downloads.deleteConfirm: Delete {{count}} downloaded file(s), {{size}} in all? Your mod list doesn't change.
downloads.deleteInUseWarning: {{count}} of them belong to mods in a profile: those are downloaded again on the next Deploy (or when that profile is used).
downloads.deletedSome: Deleted {{count}} file(s); {{failed}} couldn't be deleted (see the Log)
downloads.cantDeleteListed: This file is a mod in your list: remove the mod to delete it
downloads.addBackTip: Add this mod to the current profile again (no download needed while this file is its newest version)
downloads.state.inUseTip: A mod in one of your profiles uses this file (Deploy installs it from here)
downloads.state.olderTip: Left over after the mod was updated. Not needed unless you want to go back to this version
downloads.state.backupTip: Only a profile backup has this mod; restoring the backup uses this file
downloads.state.unlistedTip: The mod was removed from every profile. Keep it to add the mod back without downloading, or delete it
downloads.keepOldLabel: When a mod is updated, its previous file:
downloads.keepRemovedLabel: When a mod is removed from every profile, its files:
downloads.keepHint: Kept files show up below, so you can always delete them later. Files of mods in a profile backup are kept either way.
downloads.folderHint: mod.io, Nexus Mods and ModCat files. Deploy installs your mods from here. Change the folder in Settings → Download folder.
downloads.pakhubHint: Files added from Pak Hub-style repositories, kept in MINTCAT's data folder. A file whose mod is in a list is that mod, so it can only go by removing the mod.
downloads.imagesLabel: Pictures (thumbnails and avatars in Browse Mods)
downloads.imagesClearConfirm: Delete the saved thumbnails and avatars? They're downloaded again when Browse Mods shows them.
browse.addAgainTip: Already in your list (adding it again only updates it)
browse.inYourListTip: This mod is in the current profile
browse.inYourListFolderTip: This mod is in the current profile, in {{folder}}
browse.inOtherProfilesTip: Not in the current profile; in: {{names}}
support.trackTip: Track on Nexus Mods (get notified about updates on Nexus). Doesn't change anything in MINTCAT.
support.untrackTip: You track this on Nexus Mods. Click to stop tracking.
support.endorseTip: Endorse on Nexus Mods to show the author support. Nexus only accepts endorsements of mods your account has downloaded.
support.abstainTip: You endorsed this on Nexus Mods. Click to take the endorsement back.
support.subscribeTip: Subscribe on mod.io. MINTCAT doesn't need this to use the mod. If you're signed in to mod.io inside the game, the game installs subscribed mods too.
support.unsubscribeTip: You're subscribed on mod.io. Click to unsubscribe (the mod stays in MINTCAT).
support.likeTip: Like on mod.io to show the author support.
support.unlikeTip: You liked this on mod.io. Click to remove the like.
support.undislikeTip: You disliked this on mod.io. Click to remove the dislike.
support.needNexusKeyShort: (Needs your Nexus API key in User Settings.)
support.needModioTokenShort: (Needs your mod.io token in User Settings.)
support.needNexusKey: Tracking and endorsing use your Nexus Mods account. Add your personal API key in User Settings (avatar at the top right) and try again.
support.needModioToken: Subscribing and rating use your mod.io account. Add a mod.io token with read and write access in User Settings (avatar at the top right) and try again.
support.endorsed: Endorsed {{name}} on Nexus Mods. Thanks for supporting the author!
support.abstainFailed: Couldn't take back the endorsement of {{name}}
support.nexusNotDownloaded: Nexus Mods says your account hasn't downloaded this mod yet, and it only accepts endorsements of downloaded mods. Download it from Nexus (adding it in MINTCAT through Nexus counts), then try again.
support.nexusTooSoon: Nexus Mods says it's too soon after downloading. Endorsements open a little while after the download, so try again later.
support.nexusOwnMod: Nexus Mods doesn't let you endorse your own mods.
support.nexusKeyRejected: Nexus Mods didn't accept your API key. Check it in User Settings.
support.modioReadOnly: mod.io didn't accept the change. Your mod.io token may only allow reading, or it has expired. On mod.io, open your account's API access page, create an OAuth token with read and write access, and paste it in User Settings.
support.modioInactive: mod.io says your account isn't active yet. Confirm your email with mod.io first.
support.modioTooMany: mod.io got too many requests. Wait a minute and try again.
notes.placeholder: Anything you want to remember about this mod: load order, settings, why it's off…
notes.hint: Only on this computer. A mod in several profiles shows the same note. Hover the note icon in the list to read it.
notes.removeText: The note is deleted. This can't be undone.
req.nexusTip: Requirements listed on the mod's Nexus page. Green ones are already in your list.
req.modioAutoTip: mod.io dependencies. MINTCAT adds these along with the mod.
req.pakhubTip: Mods the author says this one needs (found in the post's text). Green ones are already in your list.
req.authorNotesTitle: What the author wrote about requirements, load order and compatibility
req.namedHint: Named in the post without a link. Search for it on Browse Mods.
req.discordHint: Links to a Discord message that isn't a Pak Hub post MINTCAT can find. Open it to see what it is.
req.externalHint: Not something MINTCAT can add. Open the page to get it.
req.pageNeeds: The mod's page lists these as needed:
req.authorMentions: The author also mentions (not ticked, they may only be related):
help.columnsView: Shows column titles over the mod list and keeps each mod's tags and flags (your note, endorsed / liked, tracked / subscribed) in aligned columns. Off: the flags sit right after the tags, only where a mod has one.
modList.colNoteTip: Note: your note on the mod (click it to edit).
modList.colSupportTip: Endorsed on Nexus Mods / liked or disliked on mod.io, then tracked on Nexus Mods / subscribed on mod.io. Right-click a mod to change them.
help.logsKeep: Every launch gets its own log, and the Log panel's entries are saved with it. This many launches are kept; the oldest are deleted as new launches start. Only MINTCAT's own log files are deleted.
log.launchTip: Show the Log panel of an earlier launch
log.noFullLog: There's no full log file for this launch.
log.onlyFullLog: Only the full log file was kept for this launch. Click Full log to open it.
log.legacyOnlyFullLog: Builds before this one kept everything in one big log file. Click Full log to open it.
